**My reasoning:**

My family has worked this land in Quzhou for generations. I know what grows here and what sells. The soil is flat and the wells still reach water. My husband spends most of the year doing construction work in Shijiazhuang, so I manage the 10 mu mostly by myself, with my mother-in-law helping during busy periods.

There is really only one way I farm here: wheat in winter, maize in summer. Every family on our lane does the same. When I was young my father did it, and his father before him. The grain station still buys both at a stable price, and the input shops in town stock exactly what I need for these two crops.

For wheat, I will rotary-till after the maize harvest in October, then sow. I buy the improved seed from Old Zhang's shop in the village — same kind I used last year, it did well. I spread compound fertilizer before sowing and add urea around the Qingming festival when the plants are jointing. I irrigate four times: once right after sowing to help germination, once in early spring when growth picks up, once at jointing, once at heading. If I skip any of these I know the yield drops badly. I spray twice for weeds early, and once more later if I see rust or aphids.

For maize I plant directly into the stubble right after wheat harvest in June — no time to plough, the season is short. I buy hybrid seed, Zhengdan 958 or whatever the shop has that everyone is using. Summer rains help, so I only irrigate if July is very dry. I apply fertilizer twice and spray for fall armyworm if I see the leaves chewed.

I do not try anything new this year. New things cost money and I cannot afford a bad harvest.
